A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GestureHYDRA study and contain complete, readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C. The material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original SHOW and Streamer evaluations, component ablations, gesture-injection experiments, and a user study in Appendix B.1.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including the benchmark comparisons, ablations, and appendix user study.

M1.justification: The hybrid-modality diffusion transformer, four masking strategies, motion-style injection, training losses, and cascaded retrieval with adaptive timestamp selection remain unchanged in Section 3.

E1.justification: Both versions use SHOW and the Mandarin Streamer dataset, with the same seen/unseen identity scenarios, downstream video-generation example, and appendix gesture-editing demonstrations.

E2.justification: TalkSHOW, ProbTalk, and DiffuseStyleGesture remain the comparators in Tables 1, 2, and 6 and Figure 4. The ablation and injection comparison variants are also unchanged; added citations introduce no evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Dataset splits, training budgets, sampling procedures, and evaluation metrics are unchanged. Both retain 450 clips from each Streamer test split for SAR/SMD evaluation and the appendix user study with 17 examples and 20 volunteers.

E4.justification: Sections 4.4–4.5 retain the same masking, motion-style, keypoint-loss, and adaptive-injection analyses. Figure 5 and Appendix B.2 retain the same downstream-video and gesture-editing examples.

E5.justification: Both versions retain point-score reporting without repeated-run counts, random-seed disclosures, error bars, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. The user-study reporting is unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings are retained. For example, Table 1 reports GestureHYDRA FGD values of 3.24 and 15.43 for seen and unseen identities in both versions; Tables 2–4 and 6 also retain every result entry.

T1.justification: The diffusion formulation, fusion and style-attention equations, and weighted training loss remain unchanged. No mathematical definitions, derivations, assumptions, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: Streamer, hybrid-modality gesture generation with motion-style injection, and synchronized retrieval-based gesture editing. Performance and generalization claims retain their scope.

C2.justification: Explanations of semantic activation, rhythm alignment, and generalization are unchanged. Appendix C retains the same limitations concerning omitted facial reconstruction and dependence on accurate speech recognition.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 and Appendix A retain the same hardware, training schedule, sampling settings, reconstruction pipeline, and annotation instructions. The project-page address is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 adds six references, including DiffusionDet, visual autoregressive modeling, and S3O, and removes the foundational LSTM reference. It emphasizes VQ-VAE and diffusion models as mainstream approaches, while retaining the paper's substantive distinctions from previous gesture-generation methods.

P1.justification: Section 2.1 receives a limited background rewrite, Section 2.2 receives wording corrections, and several grammatical or punctuation errors are fixed elsewhere. The section order and overall narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Expanded background and references cause local column and page reflow, particularly on pages 2–4 and 9–11. Figures 1–11 and Tables 1–6 retain their visual content, organization, and captions.

improvement.justification: v2 resolves the visibly unresolved citation in Section 2.1 and corrects several awkward sentences, modestly improving citation completeness and readability. The gains are editorial: the method, experimental evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations remain unchanged.
